nom: Buttah Skin Tinted Mineral Sunscreen SPF 30

segments.oily: One reviewer with brown oily skin reports no pilling and good wear under matte foundation.
segments.dry: One dry-skin reviewer found the matte finish unsuited to her skin and layered a separate hydrating sunscreen over it, while another with combo/dry skin reported no breakouts and a moisturizing, non-tacky feel.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers are split: one reports easy pilling and flaking that prevents wearing blush or foundation over it, while another with breakout-prone combo/dry skin reports no issues and a moisturizing feel.

concerns.blemishes: One reviewer with breakout-prone, combo/dry skin reports no new breakouts or skin issues from this product.

aspects.libelle: No white cast on medium to dark skin
Poor layering under foundation or makeup
Warm tint may oxidize or suit fair skin poorly

extraits.texte: This product leaves no white cast and has a matte finish which is a plus however it pills very easily and flakes off throughout the day. Due to this, I am unable to apply any sort of blush/ highlight/ etc. after application as it will cause the sunscreen to flake off which is clearly not ideal. For reference I have combination skin.

As a Latina with brown oily skin type that likes to try new mineral sunscreens for people of color would totally recommend this sunscreen under makeup. Did not have any issues with pilling and wore beautifully under my matte foundations!

I bought this to replace a discontinued mineral sunscreen that I loved and I really do like this formula. The pros are that it's thin, not chalky, feels moisturizing but doesn't stay tacky on the skin, and has a decent ingredient list. I haven't noticed it causing any skin issues for my breakout prone, combo/dry skin. My skin tone is light/medium currently but I do get more tanned in the summer and I appreciate a tinted product. It is definitely different from the tint you might find in a tinted moisturizer in that it basically blends into nothing on your skin and is there only to mitigate any white cast from the physical sunscreen. It doesn't look "makeup-y" in any way or like you're wearing bronzer (something I've noticed in other tinted sunscreens.) The one con I have is that I can't get it to layer well with my liquid foundation and cream base products. It seems to work ok on top of my skincare, but as soon as I apply foundation I start to notice a very fine pilling on the skin - almost powdery. I even tried mixing my foundation into the sunscreen to create a tinted moisturizer and they didn't play well that way either. It could totally just be my choice of foundation, but it's worth mentioning. Overall, I appreciate brands that create this type of sunscreen and wish more brands would focus on simple and effective products. Maybe it's better on its own, but overall it's a great sunscreen.
I have dry skin and really wanted to try this out but I didn't know it gave a matte finish so I follow it up with a water resistant sunscreen from black girl sunscreen.

Product doesn't absorb well and just sits on top of skin causing product flaking. I've used other sunscreens with better absorption. I love all the other products from this line, but I'll have to go with a different brand for the SPF

I bought this sunscreen along with the Supergoop unseen sunscreen and I am returning the supergoop sunscreen and keeping this one. I have medium skin and this doesn't leave a white cast. I love that it works well with my skincare and under my makeup. I haven't had no issues with it pilling on me or it making my face look extra greasy. I wish that it had a higher spf but I will still be repurchasing.
It doesn't create a cast and is a perfect match for my skin but at the price paid, the packaging is terrible. The product comes out at the seam on the side where the label stops.
